clue.text: Plays a guitar for drinks on the street

parts.note: rums are glasses of the spirit, so drinks

explanation.surface: A busker strums for the price of a drink on the pavement.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the drinks sit on top, but here ST simply comes first, the drinks following it.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumming is sweeping the fingers across the strings, the usual way of playing a guitar casually.

clue.text: It gives warning to sailors affected by the drink

definitions.text: It gives warning to sailors affected by the drink

parts.words: It gives warning to sailors affected by the drink
parts.note: the drink is slang for the sea; a floating marker whose bell rings as the waves rock it warns sailors

explanation.surface: Something that alerts drunken sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected by the drink' suggests drunkenness, but the drink is the sea, whose motion sounds the bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigation marker fitted with a bell that is rung by wave motion, warning ships of hazards.

clue.text: Sharpens games up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: sports are games

explanation.surface: Someone hones their skills or raises the level of their games.
explanation.definitionFit: To strop a razor is to sharpen it on a leather strap.

clue.text: Study bill for dispatch

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
a bill is a poster, a kind of sign

explanation.surface: Someone examines an invoice before sending it off.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign goods is to send or dispatch them to someone.

clue.text: Control river pests

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
lice are parasitic pests

explanation.surface: A call to deal with vermin infesting a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To police something is to keep it in order or control it.

clue.text: Decline to visit daughter

parts.note: to go to see someone is to visit them
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: Refusing an invitation to call on one's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like 'refuse', but it means deteriorate.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that run to seed are past their best, so the idiom means to deteriorate or decline.

clue.text: Army command to be rigidly obeyed

definitions.text: Army command to be rigidly obeyed

parts.words: Army command to be rigidly obeyed
parts.note: the parade-ground order makes soldiers stand stiffly upright, so it is literally obeyed rigidly

explanation.surface: An order that must be followed to the letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rigidly' seems to mean strictly, but soldiers obey this order by standing rigid.
explanation.definitionFit: The drill command for soldiers to stand straight with heels together and arms at their sides.

clue.text: Two officers get together for a drink

indicators.note: two signals that the officer abbreviation is written twice in a row

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A pair of officers meet up for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot beverage made from powdered cacao beans, usually with milk.

clue.text: Packed audience gives a good hand

definitions.meaning: a theatre with every seat sold is said to have this
in poker, three of a kind plus a pair, a strong hand

explanation.surface: A sold-out crowd applauds generously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good hand' suggests applause; it is a poker hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a sold-out theatre and a poker hand of three matching cards with a pair.

clue.text: Turf out? Of course

parts.note: a piece of turf knocked out of a golf course by a club swing

explanation.surface: Someone agrees heartily that a person should be thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turf out' reads as evict and 'Of course' as naturally; really it is turf out of a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A chunk of grass and earth gouged out by a golfer's stroke.

clue.text: Constantly right

definitions.meaning: faithful, steady; the adverb sense is loyally

explanation.walkthrough: 'Constantly' is taken in the sense of steadfast loyalty, as in 'remain true'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both loyal steadiness and factual correctness.

clue.text: Children produced periodically

definitions.meaning: editions of a magazine or journal put out at intervals

explanation.surface: Kids born at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal word for offspring, and also the numbered editions of a periodical.

clue.text: Gardener cultivated and gathered in crops

indicators.note: cultivated soil is worked over, so the letters of the word before are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener tended plants and brought in the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated' seems to be the gardener's work; it signals rearranging GARDENER.
explanation.definitionFit: To garner is to gather and store grain or other harvest.

clue.text: Wishes of a worshipful company

definitions.meaning: what a congregation at worship says together

explanation.surface: The desires of a livery company, a London trade guild styled 'Worshipful'.
explanation.walkthrough: London's old trade guilds are styled 'Worshipful Company of ...', but here the company is a congregation at worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest requests, and the petitions offered by a congregation at worship.

clue.text: Preparing for exam? That makes a change

definitions.meaning: going back over study material before a test

explanation.surface: A student's cramming seen as a welcome change of habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both studying again before a test and an altered or amended version.

clue.text: Put to flight right away

parts.note: someone away is out, not at home

explanation.surface: Someone scared off immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' reads as immediately but splits into R and OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To rout an army is to defeat it decisively and send it fleeing.

clue.text: Inferior articles that don't last long

definitions.meaning: goods sold cheaply because of flaws

explanation.surface: Shoddy goods that soon fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests poor goods wearing out, but the second sense is units of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both flawed goods sold at a discount and brief units of time.

clue.text: It comes in to resist, or just the contrary

indicators.note: comes in says the word It enters the middle of the synonym for resist

parts.note: to oppose is to resist
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something arrives to fight back, or does quite the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completely contrary is diametrically different.

clue.text: Money coming in from flat in French street

indicators.note: in places the level word inside the French word for street

parts.note: rue is French for street
even means flat or level

explanation.surface: Rental income from an apartment in a Paris street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' suggests an apartment, fitting the property surface; it means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Income, especially that received by a government or business.

clue.text: Proposal to provide public with running water

parts.note: overt means open, public
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, so a stretch of running water

explanation.surface: A plan to bring piped water to the people.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a North Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening approach or offer made to start negotiations.

clue.text: Managed to get detectives' rank …

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Someone engineered a promotion within the detective force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a police grade; it means foul-smelling. CID is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank, as an adjective, means foul-smelling, as rancid butter is.

clue.text: Former model makes a revelation

parts.note: ex means former
to pose is to model, as for an artist

explanation.surface: An ex-model spills secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of journalism that reveals scandal is a disclosure.

clue.text: … and manage to avoid a leakage

definitions.meaning: to get away from or evade

explanation.surface: The detectives, continuing from the previous clue, dodge a leak of information.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to 21 down; the clues are solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Both evading something and a leak of gas or fluid.

clue.text: The bishop's concern observed in child's play

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, the area in his charge
saw means observed

explanation.surface: A bishop watches children playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child's play' suggests something easy; it is a playground plank toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A balanced plank on which children rock up and down, a playground toy.

clue.text: Exercising we object to in middle age

parts.note: us is the object form of we

indicators.note: middle picks the central letter of the word age

explanation.surface: Taking up exercise in middle age and grumbling about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We object' reads as a complaint; it is grammar: us is the object case of we.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercising a right or skill means putting it to use.

clue.text: Queen's favourite isle? Crete, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters given may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Crete is the queen's preferred island.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was famously Elizabeth I's favourite courtier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of Leicester was Queen Elizabeth I's favourite, so the title stands for him.

clue.text: Funny business with three blind victims?

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: the rhyme's mice were victims of the farmer's wife, who cut off their tails, so the creatures lose their final letter

parts.note: the nursery rhyme's three blind mice

explanation.surface: Something odd is going on involving three sightless sufferers.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cuts off the tails of the three blind mice; 'victims' signals MICE losing its tail, leaving MIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic is a synonym of funny, meaning causing laughter.

clue.text: Meat market's up for relocation

indicators.note: relocation moves things to new places, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A meat market is going up for a move to new premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef from the hindquarters, a type of steak.
